problems.problem: Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with $AB=1$. Suppose that $K$ is a point on the side $AD$ such that $KD=1$, $\angle ABK=90^{\circ}$ and $\angle DBK=30^{\circ}$. Determine $AD$.
Prove that among any four distinct numbers from the interval $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ there are two, say $x,y$, such that $$8 \cos x \cos y \cos (x-y)+1>4(\cos^2 x+\cos^2 y).$$
In space $1997$ points are given. Let $M$ and $m$ be the largest and the smallest distance between two of the given points. Prove that $\frac{M}{m}>9$.
The equation $ax^3+bx^2+cx+d=0$ has three distinct real solutions. How many distinct real solutions does the following equation have: $$4(ax^3+bx^2+cx+d)(3ax+b)=(3ax^2+2bx+c)^2?$$
Find all real solutions of the equation $$(2+\sqrt{3})^x+1=\left( 2\sqrt{2+\sqrt{3}} \right)^x.$$
Determine the smallest natural number $n$ such that among any $n$ integers one can choose $18$ integers whose sum is divisible by $18$.

On the edges $AB,BC,CD,DA$ of a parallelepiped $ABCDA_1B_1C_1D_1$ points $K,L,M,N$ are selected, respectively. Prove that the circumcenters of the tetrahedra $A_1AKN$, $B_1BKL$, $C_1CLM$, $D_1DMN$ are the vertices of a parallelogram.
Solve the equation $\sqrt{1+\{2x\}}=\lfloor x^2\rfloor+2\lfloor x\rfloor+3$, where $\{a\}=a-\lfloor a\rfloor$.

The altitude $CD$ of triangle $ABC$ meets the bisector $BK$ of this triangle at $M$ and the altitude $KL$ of triangle $BKC$ at $N$. The circumcircle of triangle $BKN$ meets the side $AB$ at a point $P\ne B$. Prove that the triangle $KPM$ is isosceles.
Prove that for any numbers $0<x,y,z\le1$ $$\frac x{1+y+zx}+\frac y{1+z+xy}+\frac z{1+x+yz}\le\frac3{x+y+z}.$$

Consider a function $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$. Suppose that there is a real number $0<\lambda<1$ such that $f(\lambda)\notin\{0,\lambda\}$ and the equality $$f(f(x)+y)=f(x)+f(y)$$ holds whenever the function is defined at the arguments.

(a) Give an example of such a function.

(b) Prove that for some $x\in[0,1]$ $$\underbrace{f(f(\cdots f}_{19}(x)\cdots))=\underbrace{f(f(\cdots f}_{98}(x)\cdots)).$$
Find the number of real roots of the equation $$\frac2\pi\arccos x=\sqrt{1-x^2}+1.$$

The numbers $1$, $1998$, $1999$ are written on the board. In each step it is allowed to replace one of the numbers by its square decreased by three times the product of the other two numbers. Is it possible to obtain three numbers with sum $0$ after several steps?

Two spheres are externally tangent at a point $P$. The segments $AB$ and $CD$ touch both spheres, with $A$ and $C$ lying on the first sphere and $B$ and $D$ on the second. Let $M$ and $N$ be the projections of the midpoints of the segments $AC$ and $BD$ on the line joining the centers of the spheres. Prove that $PM=PN$.

The sequence $(x_n)$ is given by $x_1=1$ and $$x_{n+1}=\frac{n^2}{x_n}+\frac{x_n}{n^2}+2\quad\text{for }n\ge1.$$ (a) Prove that $x_{n+1}\ge x_n$ for all $n\ge4$.

(b) Prove that $\lfloor x_n\rfloor=n$ for all $n\ge4$.
Find all values of the parameter $k$ for which the system of inequalities $$\begin{cases}ky^2+4ky-2x+6k+3\le0\\ kx^2-2y-2kx+3k-3\le0\end{cases}$$ has a unique solution.

All faces of a parallelepiped $ABCDA_1B_1C_1D_1$ are rhombi, and their angles at $A$ are all equal to $\alpha$. Points $M,N,P,Q$ are selected on the edges $A_1B_1,DC,BC,A_1D_1$, respectively, such that $A_1M=BP$ and $DN=A_1Q$. Find the angle between the lines of intersection of the plane $A_1BD$ with the planes $AMN$ and $APQ$.

Two players alternately write integers on a blackboard as follows: the first player writes $a_1$ arbitrarily, then the second player writes $a_2$ arbitrarily, and thereafter a player writes a number equal to the sum of the two preceding numbers. The player after whose move the obtained sequence contains terms $a_i, a_j, a_{i+1}, a_{j+1}$ $(i\ne j)$ such that $a_i-a_j$ and $a_{i+1}-a_{j+1}$ are divisible by $1999$ wins the game. Which of the players has a winning strategy?
Can the number (a) $19991998$, (b) $19991999$ be written in the form $n^4+m^3-m$, where $n$ and $m$ are integers?
Find all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that $$f(xy)+f(xz)-f(x)f(yz)\ge1\qquad\text{for all }x,y,z.$$

Suppose that the function $f(x)=\tan(a_1x+1)+\ldots+\tan(a_{10}x+1)$ has period $T>0$, where $a_1,\ldots,a_{10}$ are positive numbers. Prove that $$T\ge\frac\pi{10}\min\left\{\frac1{a_1},\ldots,\frac1{a_{10}}\right\}.$$

Let $AA_1,BB_1,CC_1$ be the altitudes of an acute-angled triangle $ABC$, and let $O$ be an arbitrary interior point. Let $M,N,P,Q,R,S$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $O$ to the lines $AA_1,BC,BB_1,CA,CC_1,AB$, respectively. Prove that the lines $MN,PQ,RS$ are concurrent.
Solve in $\mathbb{R}$ the equation $$\left| x-\frac{\pi}{6} \right|+\left| x+\frac{\pi}{3} \right|=\arcsin \frac{x^3-x+2}{2}.$$
The sum of positive real numbers $a,b,c$ equals $1$. Prove that $$\sqrt{\frac{1}{a}-1}\sqrt{\frac{1}{b}-1}+\sqrt{\frac{1}{b}-1}\sqrt{\frac{1}{c}-1}+\sqrt{\frac{1}{c}-1}\sqrt{\frac{1}{a}-1} \ge 6.$$

In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$, $\omega$ is the circumcircle and $O$ its center, $\omega_1$ is the circumcircle of triangle $AOC$, and $OQ$ is a diameter of $\omega_1$. Let $M$ and $N$ be points on the lines $AQ$ and $AC$ respectively such that the quadrilateral $AMBN$ is a parallelogram. Prove that the lines $MN$ and $BQ$ intersect on $\omega_1$.
Find all monotone (not necessarily strictly) functions $f: [0,+\infty)\to \mathbb{R}$ such that $$f(x+y)-f(x)-f(y)=f(xy+1)-f(xy)-f(1)\quad\text{for all } x,y \ge 0$$ and $$f(3)+3f(1)=3f(2)+f(0).$$
Find all positive integers $n$ for which $\cos \left(\pi \sqrt{n^2+n}\right) \ge 0$.
A polygon on a coordinate grid is built of $2005$ dominoes $1 \times 2$. What is the smallest number of sides of even length that such a polygon can have?
Prove that for every integer $n \ge 2$ there is a set $A_n$ of $n$ distinct positive integers such that for any two distinct elements $i,j \in A_n$, $|i-j|$ divides $i^2+j^2$.

In space $2005$ points are marked, no four of which lie in the same plane. A plane is drawn through every three of the points. Show that the points can be painted in two colors so that for any two points of the same color the number of drawn planes separating them is odd. (Two points are separated by a plane if they lie in different open half-spaces determined by the plane.)
Find all real values of $a$ for which the system of equations $$\begin{cases}x+y+z=0\\ xy+yz+azx=0\end{cases}$$ has exactly one solution.

Let $M = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48\}$. Find out which four-element subsets of $M$ are more numerous: those for which the product of all elements is greater than $2009$, or those for which the product of all elements is less than $2009$.

In triangle $ABC$ let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of $BC$ and $AC$, respectively. Point $P$ inside $ABC$ is such that $\angle BAP = \angle PBC = \angle PCA$. Prove that if $\angle PNA = \angle AMB$, then $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle.

Find all polynomials $P(x)$ with real coefficients such that for all pairwise distinct positive integers $x, y, z, t$ with $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 2t^2$ and $\gcd(x, y, z, t) = 1$, the following equality holds: $$2P^2(t) + 2P(xy + yz + zx) = P^2(x + y + z).$$ Here $P^2(k)=\left(P(k)\right)^2$.
Solve the system of equations $$\begin{cases}x^3=2y^3+y-2\\ y^3=2z^3+z-2\\ z^3 = 2x^3+x-2.\end{cases}$$
Find all functions $f : \mathbb Z \to \mathbb Z$ such that $$f(n|m|) + f(n(|m|+2)) = 2f(n(|m|+1))\qquad\text{for all } m,n \in \mathbb Z.$$
Point $O$ inside triangle $ABC$ is such that $\angle AOB = \angle BOC = \angle COA = 120^\circ$. Prove that $$\frac{AO^2}{BC}+\frac{BO^2}{CA}+\frac{CO^2}{AB} \geq \frac{AO+BO+CO}{\sqrt 3}.$$

Let $G$ be a connected graph in which every vertex has degree at least $m \geq 3$, such that there is no path passing through every vertex of $G$ exactly once. Find the least possible number of vertices of $G$.
Find all triples of pairwise distinct positive integers $(a,b,c)$ which satisfy the following conditions: $2a-1$ is divisible by $b$, $2b-1$ is divisible by $c$ and $2c-1$ is divisible by $a$.

In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$, $AH$ is an altitude and $AM$ is a median. Points $X$ and $Y$ on the lines $AB$ and $AC$ respectively are such that $AX=XC$ and $AY=YB$. Prove that the midpoint of $XY$ is equidistant from $H$ and $M$.
Find all functions $f:[0,+\infty) \to [0,+\infty)$ which for all nonnegative $x,y$ satisfy $$f(f(x)+f(y))=xyf(x+y).$$

Two players, Andriy and Olesya, play the following game. On a table there is a round cake, which is cut by one of the players into $2n$ ($n>1$) sectors (pieces) of pairwise distinct weights. The weight of each piece is known to both players. Then they take pieces according to the following rules. First Olesya takes $1$ piece, then Andriy takes $2$ pieces such that the remaining pieces form a sector. Then they take turns, each taking $2$ pieces such that after each turn the remaining pieces form a sector. In the last move, one of the players takes the one remaining piece. Each player aims to get more cake than the opponent. For which $n$ can Olesya cut the cake so that she wins, if in her first move she takes the smallest piece?

A squadron of $10$ powerful destroyers and $20$ small boats is about to attack an island. All ships are positioned on a straight line and are equally spaced.

Two torpedo boats with $10$ torpedoes each want to protect the island. However, the first torpedo boat can shoot only at $10$ successive ships, whereas the second one can shoot at $10$ targets each of which is next but one to the previous. They have to shoot at the same moment, so some targets may be hit by both torpedo boats.

What is the largest number of destroyers that can be guaranteed to avoid the torpedoes, no matter which targets the torpedo boats choose?

The sequence $(x_n)$ is given by $x_1=a$, $x_{n+1}=\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x_n-\dfrac{1}{x_n}\right)$. Prove that there is $a$ such that the sequence $(x_n)$ has exactly $2018$ pairwise distinct elements. (If some element of the sequence is equal to $0$, the sequence stops at that element.)

Given $N$ positive integers such that the greatest common divisors of all nonempty subsets of them are pairwise distinct. What is the smallest possible number of prime factors of the product of all $N$ numbers?

Given an acute-angled triangle $ABC$, let $AA_1$ and $CC_1$ be its angle bisectors, $I$ its incenter, and $M$ and $N$ the midpoints of $AI$ and $CI$. Points $K$ and $L$ in the interior of triangles $AC_1I$ and $CA_1I$ respectively are such that $\angle AKI = \angle CLI = \angle AIC$, $\angle AKM = \angle ICA$, $\angle CLN = \angle IAC$. Prove that the circumradii of triangles $KIL$ and $ABC$ are equal.

It is known that for some integers $a_{2021},a_{2020},\dots,a_1,a_0$ the expression $$a_{2021}n^{2021}+a_{2020}n^{2020}+\dots+a_1n+a_0$$ is divisible by $2021$ for every integer $n$. Must each of the numbers $a_{2021},a_{2020},\dots,a_1,a_0$ also be divisible by $2021$?
Find all natural numbers $n \ge 3$ for which in an arbitrary $n$-gon one can choose $3$ vertices dividing its boundary into three parts whose lengths can be the side lengths of a triangle.

Let $O, I, H$ be the circumcenter, the incenter and the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$. The lines $AI$ and $AH$ meet the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ for the second time at $D$ and $E$, respectively. Prove that if $OI \parallel BC$, then the circumcenter of triangle $OIH$ lies on $DE$.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for all real $x,y$ $$f(xf(x+y))+f((x+y)f(y))=(x+y)^2.$$
Are there natural numbers $m,n,k$ that satisfy the equation $m^m+ n^n=k^k$?

The altitudes $AA_1$, $BB_1$ and $CC_1$ are drawn in the triangle $ABC$. Point $K$ is the projection of point $B$ on $A_1C_1$. Prove that the symmedian of triangle $ABC$ from the vertex $B$ bisects the segment $B_1K$.

A natural number $n$ is given. Prove that one can choose $\varphi(n)+1$ (not necessarily different) divisors of $n$ with sum $n$.

Here $\varphi(n)$ denotes the number of natural numbers less than $n$ that are coprime with $n$.

There are $101$ not necessarily different weights, each of which weighs an integer number of grams from $1$ g to $2020$ g. It is known that for any division of these weights into two heaps, the total weight of at least one of the heaps is at most $2020$ g. What is the largest possible total weight of all $101$ weights?
A set $M$ contains $n \ge 2$ positive integers. It is known that for any two different $a, b \in M$, $a^2+1$ is divisible by $b$. What is the largest possible value of $n$?

Points $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_{2022}$ are chosen in a plane so that no three of them are collinear. Consider all angles $A_iA_jA_k$ for distinct points $A_i, A_j, A_k$. What is the largest possible number of these angles that can be equal to $90^\circ$?

In the quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle ABC = \angle CDA = 90^\circ$. Let $P = AC \cap BD$, $Q = AB\cap CD$, $R = AD \cap BC$. Let $\ell$ be the midline of the triangle $PQR$ parallel to $QR$. Show that the circumcircle of the triangle formed by the lines $AB, AD, \ell$ is tangent to the circumcircle of the triangle formed by the lines $CD, CB, \ell$.
Find all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all real $x, y$ $$f(x+yf(x+y)) = f(y^2) + xf(y) + f(x).$$
Let us call a polynomial mixed if it has both positive and negative coefficients ($0$ is considered neither positive nor negative). Is the product of two mixed polynomials always mixed?

Let $K$ be the midpoint of the median $AM$ of a triangle $ABC$. Points $X, Y$ lie on $AB, AC$, respectively, such that $\angle KXM =\angle ACB$, $AX>BX$, and similarly $\angle KYM =\angle ABC$, $AY>CY$. Prove that $B, C, X, Y$ are concyclic.

For a positive integer $n$ consider all its divisors $1 = d_1 < d_2 < \ldots < d_k = n$. For $2 \le i \le k-1$, call the divisor $d_i$ good if $d_{i-1}d_{i+1}$ is not divisible by $d_i$. Find all $n$ such that the number of their good divisors is smaller than the number of their distinct prime divisors.

There are $2024$ cities in a country, every two of which are connected in both directions by exactly one of three modes of transportation: rail, air or road. A tourist has arrived in this country and has the entire transportation scheme. He chooses a travel ticket for one of the modes of transportation and the city from which he starts his trip. He wants to visit as many cities as possible, using only the ticket for the chosen mode of transportation. What is the largest $k$ for which the tourist will always be able to visit at least $k$ cities? During the route he may return to cities he has already visited.

Find all pairs of positive integers $a, b$ for which the following equality holds:
$$(a, b) + 3 \cdot [a, b] = a^3 - b^3.$$
Here $(a, b)$ and $[a, b]$ denote the greatest common divisor and the least common multiple of the positive integers $a, b$, respectively.

Let positive integers $m$ and $n$ greater than $1$ be given. Vasyl and Petro play a game in which they take turns marking points $(x, y)$ in the coordinate plane, where $x, y$ are positive integers satisfying $1 \le x \le m$, $1 \le y \le n$.

The player after whose move there appear two marked points whose distance is not a positive integer loses. Who wins if Vasyl starts the game?

Define the almost arithmetic mean of a collection of numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ as the quantity $\frac{a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n}{n+1}$. There is a collection $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_{2023}$ of positive, not necessarily distinct numbers. For each pair of indices $(i, j)$ with $1 \le i \le j \le 2023$, Oleksii wrote on the board the almost arithmetic mean of the numbers $b_i, b_{i+1}, \dots, b_j$.

Prove that there are at least $45$ pairwise distinct numbers on the board.

Inside a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ a point $X$ is chosen such that $\angle XBC = \angle XAD$ and $\angle XCB = \angle XDA$. The rays $AB$ and $DC$ meet at the point $O$, and the circumcircles of triangles $BCO$ and $ADO$ also meet at the point $T$. Prove that the line $TX$ and the perpendicular dropped from the point $O$ to the line $BC$ meet on the circumcircle of triangle $AOD$.

Twelve not necessarily distinct nonzero real numbers are given.

Find all positive integers $k$ from $1$ to $12$ such that among them one can always choose $k$ numbers whose sum has the same sign as their product, that is, either the sum and the product are both positive, or both negative.

The points $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ lie on a line $l$ in this order. The points $P$ and $Q$ are chosen on one side of the line $l$, and the point $R$ on the other side, such that
$$\angle APB = \angle CPD = \angle QBC = \angle QCB = \angle RAD = \angle RDA.$$
Prove that the points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ lie on one line.

In the plane, $2024$ yellow and $2024$ blue points are marked, and no three of the marked points lie on one line. Call a pair of non-negative integers $(a, b)$ nice if there is a half-plane containing exactly $a$ yellow and $b$ blue points. Points lying on the line bounding the half-plane are considered not to belong to the half-plane.

Find the smallest possible number of nice pairs.

Find all polynomials $P(n)$ with integer coefficients for each of which there exists a positive integer $N$ such that for every positive integer $n \ge N$ the number $P(n)$ is a positive integer and divides the number $n!$.

Twelve segments are given. It is known that they can be divided into $4$ groups of $3$ segments so that a triangle can be built from the segments of each triple. Can these $12$ segments always be divided into $3$ groups of $4$ segments so that a quadrilateral can be built from the segments of each quadruple?

The lines $AB$ and $CD$, on which the opposite legs of a trapezoid $ABCD$ lie, meet at the point $Q$. Inside the trapezoid $ABCD$ a point $P$ is chosen such that $\angle APB = \angle CPD$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $BPD$ and $APC$ meet for the second time on the line $PQ$.

Find all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all real numbers $x$ and $y$ the following inequality holds:
$$f\left(x^2 + 2yf(x)\right) + \left(f(y)\right)^2 \le f\left((x+y)^2\right).$$

A pair of positive integers $(a, b)$ is given. It is known that for every positive integer $n$ for which the numbers $(n - a)(n + b)$ and $n^2 - ab$ are positive, they have the same number of divisors. Must $a = b$?

Initially two constant polynomials, $0$ and $1$, were written on the board. In each subsequent operation it is allowed to add $1$ to one of the polynomials and to multiply the other one by the polynomial $45x + 2025$. Can the polynomials become equal at some moment?
Oleksii chose $11$ pairwise distinct positive integers not exceeding $2025$. Prove that among them one can choose two numbers $a < b$ such that the remainder of $b$ upon division by $a$ is even.

A triangle $ABC$ is given, and an arbitrary point $D$ is chosen on its side $AC$. In the triangles $ABD$ and $CBD$ the angle bisectors $BK$ and $BL$, respectively, are drawn. The point $O$ is the circumcentre of $\triangle KBL$. Prove that the second intersection point of the circumcircles of triangles $ABL$ and $CBK$ lies on the line $OD$.

$102$ leaders of countries came to the IMO. At the closing session, the IMO chair wants to introduce some changes to the regulations, which must be approved. To approve the changes it is necessary to obtain "for" votes from no fewer than $\frac{2}{3}$ of the participants of the vote. It is known that some leaders do not attend the session and that $81$ leaders will be present at the closing session. In the session hall the chair must seat them in the form of a $9 \times 9$ square, where each leader will sit in the $1 \times 1$ cell assigned to them. The chair knows that $28$ of these $81$ are guaranteed to support him, that is, they will always vote "for". The rest will vote as follows: in the last second of the vote they look at how their neighbours voted, that is, the leaders seated in the $1 \times 1$ cells adjacent by sides, and if the majority of them voted "for", then they also cast their vote "for", and if there is no such majority, they will vote "against".

For example, a leader sitting in a corner of the session hall has $2$ neighbours and will vote "for" only if both of them voted "for".

(a) Find out whether the IMO chair can seat his $28$ supporters so that, by voting "for" in the first second of the vote, they bring about a "for" vote of at least $\frac{2}{3}$ of all $102$ leaders;

(b) determine the largest number of "for" votes the chair can obtain by seating his $28$ supporters appropriately.
On a circle there are $2025$ real numbers. Any two adjacent numbers differ by at least $1012$. Prove that there exist two adjacent numbers whose difference is at least $1013$.

On the side $BC$ of triangle $ABC$, point $D$ is chosen such that $\angle DAB = \angle ACB$. Point $E$ is chosen on $AD$ so that $AB=2BE$. On ray $AD$ a point $F$ is chosen such that $\angle BFA = \angle EBC$. Prove that line $BE$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $CDF$.

Does there exist a prime number $p > 3$ and a permutation $\{a_1,a_2,\dots,a_{p-1}\}$ of the numbers $\{1,2,\dots,p-1\}$ such that the numbers $$a_1^{a_2},\ a_2^{a_3},\ \dots,\ a_{p-2}^{a_{p-1}},\ a_{p-1}^{a_1}$$ give pairwise distinct remainders modulo $p$?

A $(2n-1)\times(2n-1)$ board is colored black and white. In one move, one may choose any rectangle or square inside the board and invert the colors of all its cells. What is the minimum number of moves needed to guarantee that all cells become the same color?

Into what smallest number of groups can the integers from $1$ to $2026$ be partitioned so that the least common multiple of the numbers in each group does not exceed $2026$? A group may consist of a single number.

In each $1 \times 1$ cell of a $2026 \times 2026$ square there is an arrow that points in one of four directions ("up", "down", "left" or "right"). Vadym may move a token from cell $A$ to a neighboring cell $B$ (sharing a side) only if the arrow in cell $A$ points toward cell $B$.

In one press of a button, he may rotate the arrow in any chosen cell by $90^\circ$ clockwise or counterclockwise.

He wants to get from a cell $A$ to a cell $B$. Determine the minimum number of button presses that guarantees that Vadym can reach cell $B$ from cell $A$, regardless of the chosen cells $A$ and $B$ and the initial arrangement of the arrows.

Let $O$ be the circumcenter of an acute triangle $ABC$, and let $N$ be the midpoint of the larger arc $BC$ of its circumcircle. On the extension of the angle bisector $AL$ of $\angle A$, choose a point $P$ such that line $BO$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $BCP$. Let $Q$ be a point on line $PN$ lying in the same half-plane with respect to line $BC$ as $A$, and suppose $\angle BQC = 90^\circ$. Prove that line $BC$ contains the angle bisector of $\angle LPQ$.
Find all functions $f:(0,+\infty)\to(0,+\infty)$ such that for all positive $x,y$, $$y f(xf(x)) + x f(yf(y)) = f(x+y).$$
